raw_response:
I have farmed these 10.1 mu in Quzhou for 55 years. At 70, I work alone, so I must choose crops I can manage and that I know well. I will put 8 mu into my wheat-maize rotation because that is the backbone of my farm and my land is suited to it. The remaining 2.1 mu I will plant with cotton. I have grown cotton all my life and know how to handle it, even though picking is hard work for an old man.

For the winter wheat on the 8 mu, I will plant improved seeds after the National Day holiday, as I always have. Before planting, I will plough the field deep to bury the maize stubble. I will apply base fertilizer with compound fertilizer and then top-dress with urea in spring when the wheat turns green. I will irrigate three times from my well: at green-up, at jointing, and at heading. That is enough if the spring is not too dry. I will spray pesticide twice—once for aphids in spring and once for disease if I see spots on the leaves. I expect about 500 kg per mu.

For the summer maize on the same 8 mu, I must plant fast after wheat harvest in early June. I will buy hybrid maize seeds from the county shop. I will do rotary tillage quickly after the wheat comes out and plant right away. I will apply fertilizer at planting and again when the plants are at the big trumpet stage. I will irrigate twice—once when the leaves roll in the summer heat and once at grain filling. Two pesticide sprays: herbicide at planting and one insecticide if there are corn borers. I expect about 600 kg per mu.

For the 2.1 mu of cotton, I will plant improved Bt cotton seed in late April after the soil warms. I will rotary till and make ridges. Cotton needs balanced fertilizer—some compound fertilizer at planting and urea plus potassium at flowering. I will irrigate twice during flowering and boll-setting. Even with Bt seed, I will spray pesticide three times for aphids and spider mites. I will pick the cotton myself in autumn, boll by boll. I expect about 230 kg of seed cotton per mu.

This is my plan. It is not fancy, but it has kept me fed for 55 years.
